0.long_answer: Bevacizumab is a monoclonal antibody initially developed for the treatment of various cancers. It functions by inhibiting vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A), which plays a critical role in angiogenesis. By blocking VEGF-A, bevacizumab prevents the growth of new blood vessels that tumors need for growth and also offers benefits in the treatment of certain forms of retinopathy, such as age-related macular degeneration (AMD) and diabetic retinopathy, when administered via intravitreal injection.
